Subject: Dedicated sizing request & allocation for Skyline Health Q3 cluster

Hi Mina / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're moving fast on a Q3 rollout that will rely on a dedicated Redwood cluster for inference across a set of clinical triage workloads. We attached our projected utilization (skyline_capacity_request_q3.xlsx) — the short version: we need an initial committed cluster of 48 A100-equivalent GPUs starting 7/15, with predictable latency under 200ms 95th.

We understand capacity is tight across vendors; Skyline is asking Redwood for confirmation of sizing and an allocation commitment by EOD Friday (6/30) so we can finalize the procurement schedule and payroll runway. If there's any flexibility on start date or burst policy we can consider it, but we need clarity to tell Legal/Procurement.

Attachment: skyline_capacity_request_q3.xlsx (spreadsheet)

– Emily

Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing request & allocation for Skyline Health Q3 cluster

Emily — thanks for the clear ask and for the workbook. Quick summary from our side after an initial capacity check: we do not currently have 48 A100-equivalents available for new dedicated commitments starting 7/15 without impacting a small number of existing reserved customers.

Options I can propose immediately:
- Short-term compromise: carve out a 30-GPU baseline dedicated pool for Skyline on 7/15, plus access to a burst lane (best-effort, up to +10 GPUs) for high-priority traffic.
- Phased handoff: 30 GPUs on 7/15, ramp to 48 by 8/15 as planned hardware rotations complete (we can guarantee that ramp schedule).
- Equivalent-model fallback: offer 48 lower-cost T4/RTX-equivalent nodes pre-715 for non-latency-critical workloads, keep A100s for online latency-sensitive traffic.

I want to be transparent: offers above require either a short-term billing amendment or an explicit burst SLA for priority traffic. Marcus — can you weigh in on whether we can produce the 30+burst lane safely from an infra perspective and what the latency tradeoffs would be? Monica — FYI for renewal cadence / procurement messaging.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Dedicated Solutions | Redwood Inference

Appreciate the fast response, Mina. A couple of notes from account:
- Skyline is on a committed annual plan (signed Q1) for 36 committed GPUs; their Q3 ask is an expansion tied to a funded pilot. They have a firm go-live window for clinical teams.
- Procurement is pushing for an explicit commitment to 48 by 7/15 or a signed amendment with penalties; they can't accept a soft ramp without contractual language.

Proposed path: schedule an escalation call with Sales Leadership and Ops to get a one-time carve decision (we need a final by EOD Friday 6/30 to avoid delaying their PO). I'll pull Legal if we land on an amendment.

Attachment: (see Emily's spreadsheet)

Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing request & allocation for Skyline Health Q3 cluster

Quick infra readout and risk assessment:
- Current reservations and upcoming expirations: 12 GPUs in our pre-committed pool are slated to free on 7/10; another tranche of 8 GPUs free on 7/18 (hardware rotation). That gives us potential headroom for a fast 20-GPU carve if we reassign transient burst pools.
- Impact to existing customers: a direct carve of 18+ GPUs from reserved deals will materially increase latency risk for two mid-market customers that rely on 95th < 250ms SLO today. We can mitigate with temporary KV cache warming and request-level priority rules, but it is non-zero operational risk.

Compromise proposal (operational):
1) Approve an interim allocation of 30 A100-equivalent GPUs on 7/15 for Skyline with a guaranteed ramp schedule to 48 by 8/15.
2) Provide Skyline a documented burst lane (best-effort + up to 10 GPUs) for peak ramping; burst will be preemptible and not guaranteed.
3) Offer a one-time credit for Q3 equivalent to 5% of committed spend if Skyline signs an amendment by 07/07 (we'd need commercial to sign off).

Laura — can you confirm commercial on the credit and whether we can accept a DocuSign amendment on that timeline? If yes, I'll prepare the ops runbook and an SLO caveat doc.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

To: Emily Jordan <emily.jordan@skylinehealth.com>, Skyline Health Procurement <contracts@skylinehealth.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing request & allocation for Skyline Health Q3 cluster

Emily / Contracts team — thanks for your patience while we triaged this internally. We want to keep Skyline on track without jeopardizing other customers. Final decision below:

Decision (executive):
- Immediate allocation: Redwood will provision 30 A100-equivalent GPUs for Skyline starting 7/15.
- Ramp: We commit to a deterministic ramp to 48 GPUs by 2028-08-15 contingent on finalizing a signed amendment (DocuSign link below) by 2028-07-07.
- Burst lane: We will provide a preemptible burst lane up to +10 GPUs for short windows; this is best-effort and subject to preemption.
- Commercial concession: 5% credit on Q3 committed spend if amendment is executed by 07/07.

Next steps:
1) Contracts: please review and sign the amendment here: https://docusign.com/embeddedSigning/abc123 (we will also share a redline of contract_redlines_v3.pdf).
2) Ops: Marcus / Mina — proceed to create the runbook for the 30->48 ramp and publish SLO caveats to Skyline's console route.
3) Finance/Billing: apply the 5% credit if signed by 07/07 and log under deal DL-2028-0917-SKY.

Emily — if this is acceptable we'll loop Legal for the amendment and aim to get this executed quickly to avoid delaying your PO.

Best,
Laura Bennett
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
